title: Locally of finite type lifts along finite order thickenings (cartesian case)
statement: Let $S\subseteq S'$ be a finite order thickening of schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (a closed subscheme whose quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_{S'}$ satisfies $\mathcal I^{n+1}=0$ for some $n\ge0$), let $f':X'\to S'$ be a morphism of schemes and let $f:X=S\times_{S'}X'\to S$ be its base change [def-pc-base-change]. Then $f$ is locally of finite type if and only if $f'$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. (Affine-locally, by induction on $n$ reducing to $I^2=0$: if $A'\to B'$ is a ring map, $I\subseteq A'$ an ideal with $I^2=0$, and $A'/I\to B'/IB'$ is of finite type, then $A'\to B'$ is of finite type, by Nakayama's lemma applied to $A'[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'$ lifting a surjection $(A'/I)[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'/IB'$.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW (label lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian), part (2), with the first three paragraphs of its proof (base change direction; induction on the order of the thickening; reduction to affines) and 'The translation of (2) into algebra' (Nakayama, Algebra Lemma 00DV)

proof.text: If f' is locally of finite type, MorphismProperty.pullback_fst gives local finite type of pullback.fst i f' [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change, def-pc-fibre-product].

For the converse, obtain n, the closed-immersion hypothesis, and i.ker^(n+1)=bottom from the finite order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Fix arbitrary affine opens U in S' and V in X' with V contained in f' inverse image U. Put p=pullback.snd i f', q=pullback.fst i f', T=i inverse image U and W=p inverse image V. Both T and W are affine, since i and its base change p are closed immersions. The pullback equation and the containment give W contained in q inverse image T, hence W=p inverse image V intersect q inverse image T. The affine fibre-product calculation [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], in the form packaged by Mathlib's isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen and isIso_pushoutSection_iff (Morphisms/Flat.lean:234-254), gives a pushout of the four appLE maps on these opens. The map a=i.app U is surjective (Scheme.Hom.app_surjective); its kernel is I=i.ker.ideal(U) by Scheme.Hom.ker_apply [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. The map c=q.appLE T W is of finite type by the affine-pairs criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs].

In this ring pushout, write b=f'.appLE U V and J=I.map b. The first isomorphism theorem identifies the target C of the surjective map a with A/I. Let e:A/I iso C and let r:A/I to B/J be the induced quotient map. The maps k=r composed with e inverse from C to B/J and l:B to B/J commute over A, as is checked on representatives. The pushout universal property gives t:D to B/J with c followed by t=k and d followed by t=l. Since l is surjective, t is surjective. Since c is of finite type, k is of finite type (RingHom.FiniteType.comp_surjective). Composing k with the surjective isomorphism e proves that r is of finite type. These are the completely proved private helpers quotient_finiteType_of_isPushout and finiteType_quotient_appLE_of_closed_baseChange; no explicit tensor-quotient isomorphism is needed.

Evaluating i.ker^(n+1)=bottom at the affine open U gives I^(n+1)=bottom, using Scheme.IdealSheafData.ideal_pow and ideal_bot [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Apply finiteType_of_quotient_finiteType_nilpotent to b, I, this nilpotence equality and the finite-type quotient map established above [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent]. This proves finite type of f'.appLE on every affine pair, so LocallyOfFiniteType.mk gives local finite type of f' [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs].

proof_origin.place: Stacks Tag 09ZW, part (2), base-change paragraph, affine reduction and finite-type ring translation. The affine ring calculation uses the pushout universal property and a surjection to B/IB, rather than constructing a tensor-quotient isomorphism. The existing nilpotent ring lemma handles all finite orders.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 09ZW (more-morphisms.tex:334ff) part (2) and its proof, Morphisms 01T2/01T4 and Algebra 00DV. Statement kept. Proof in three steps: (1) easy direction by base change (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change = locallyOfFiniteType_isStableUnderBaseChange); (2) affine reduction: for affine U'=Spec A' ⊆ S', V'=Spec B' ⊆ X' over it, p^{-1}(V') = U ×_{U'} V' = Spec(B'/IB') over U = Spec(A'/I) (existing leaves lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra; ideal-sheaf definitions); (3) converse by 01T2 (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs = locallyOfFiniteType_iff, Mathlib's definition) and the new unsplit ring lemma lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent (A'/I → B'/IB' finite type, I nilpotent ⇒ A' → B' finite type; Nakayama 00DV (11), absent from Mathlib). The source's induction on the order of the thickening is bypassed since 00DV (11) and hence the ring lemma hold for any nilpotent ideal; the affine-open correspondence 06AD and the thickening X ⊆ X' are not needed (the affine open W is a fibre product of affines). Mathlib: only the base change direction is there.
